data.title: Crypto market rally: Why BTC and altcoins like Ethena, Injective,VeChain are rising
data.description:
A crypto market rally is happening today, September 19, with Bitcoin and top altcoins like Ethena (ENA), Injective (INJ), and VeChain (VET) rising by double digits. The market capitalization of all coins jumped by 4% in the last 24 hours to $2.78 trillion. This article explores some of the top reasons behind the cryptocurrency market rally.

Crypto market rally is happening as Bitcoin crosses $81k

One of the main reasons behind the ongoing crypto market rally is that Bitcoin has staged a strong comeback and moved above the key resistance level of $80,000. This rally is mostly because of its role as a safe-haven asset amid the ongoing US public debt surge. The debt jumped to $40 trillion and is continuing its uptrend. 

Bitcoin has unique characteristics that make it a safe-haven asset, including its supply cap of 21 million coins and the fact that it has never experienced a hack in the last 17 years of its inception. Some investors see it as the digital version of gold. 

Further, there are signs that investors have embraced a risk-on sentiment in the market, with the Crypto Fear and Greed Index remaining in the greed zone of 73. It has remained above this level in the past month, the longest streak this year. In most cases, investors tend to pile into digital coins whenever a sense of greed is in the market.

Bitcoin and altcoins are also surging as demand among investors rise. The 24-hour volume rose by 17.8% in the last 24 hours to over $104.9 billion. 

Technicals also explain why these tokens are doing well. Bitcoin has formed a bullish flag and a golden cross pattern. In most cases, these patterns normally leads to more gains over time. Other tokens like ETH, XRP, and Solana have also done that pattern.

Ethena, Injective, and Solana rising amid strong technicals

While top tokens like Ethena, Injective, and Solana have strong fundamentals, there are signs that the ongoing rebound is driven by their technicals. 

ENA token chart | Source: TradingView

As the above chart shows, ENA token soared to the crucial resistance level of $0.1908 in August and then retreated to $0.1350. Since then, it has staged a strong comeback and moved above the key resistance level of  $0.1908, confirming the bullish breakout.

The coin remains above all moving averages, while momentum indicators are rising. Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the token is bullish, with the next key target being the psychological level of $0.2500.

INJ price chart | Source: TradingView

Injective token jumped after 21Shares filed for a spot INJ ETF and as the community members voted to intensify its role in the financial industry. Technicals also explain why it is soaring today. It formed a cup-and-handle pattern, a common continuation sign in technical analysis.

It has also moved above the upper side of this cup, and remained above all moving averages. The most likely scenario is where it retests the upper side of the cup at $7.3167. These technicals suggest that it has more upside to go once the retest happens.

VET price chart | Source: TradingView

VET price has been in a strong rally in the past few months. It has remained above the 50-day moving average, which has provided it with robust support. Also, it has jumped above the key resistance level of $0.0083, its highest point on September 10. The token will likely continue rising as bulls target the psychological level of $0.01.

data.title: Trump-Xi summit: What to expect on tariffs, Taiwan, Iran and AI
data.description:
Donald Trump is set to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House next week for their second meeting this year, with the two leaders seeking to stabilise a relationship strained by trade disputes, tensions over Taiwan and Iran, and a growing rivalry over artificial intelligence.

Xi’s visit, expected on Sept. 24, will be his first to the White House in a decade and the first Chinese state visit to the United States since 2015, when he was received by then-President Barack Obama.

The summit comes at a politically consequential moment for Trump.

The US president is grappling with the Iran war, rising prices and declining popularity ahead of November’s midterm congressional elections, increasing the importance of any economic or diplomatic gains he can bring home from talks with Xi.

For China, the meeting comes as its economy remains heavily dependent on exports, with the country on track to record a trade surplus of about $1 trillion for a second consecutive year.

Beijing is likely to focus on securing access to US technology and maintaining stable trade relations while pressing Washington on Taiwan and other strategic issues.

Markets will be watching closely for signs that the two countries can extend a tariff truce that helped prevent another escalation of their trade war.

Trade truce and tariff negotiations

The October summit in South Korea produced a tariff truce that paused a confrontation in which tariffs imposed by the world's two largest economies had threatened to disrupt global supply chains.

That agreement is due to expire on November 10.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said this month that the two countries would make "some announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers".

Investors will also be looking for progress on an agreed mutual tariff reduction covering $30 billion in goods, Reuters reported.

Bloomberg reported on Tuesday that energy tariffs could be included in the $30 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts flagged after the May summit but yet to be implemented.

Such a move could pave the way for Chinese imports of US LNG to resume, with annual imports ranging from $7.5 billion to $12 billion between the end of the previous trade war in 2020 and 2024.

However, a resumption of Chinese LNG imports would not immediately translate into a major new windfall for US LNG producers.

Although Chinese imports of US LNG halted after the tariffs were imposed, Chinese buyers have continued to honour long-term contracts with US suppliers, purchasing the cargoes and then reselling them elsewhere.

China could also make a relatively straightforward move by lowering duties on US agricultural imports, potentially creating room for Washington to point to increased access for American farmers.

For Trump, such announcements could have particular political value.

He will be looking for tangible trade wins before the midterms, including high-profile purchases of US agricultural products and Boeing aircraft.

Sources told Reuters this month that Xi is preparing a large business delegation to accompany him, similar to his 2015 visit.

During that trip, China signed a $38 billion agreement for 300 Boeing aircraft.

China said after the May summit that it would buy 200 additional Boeing jets, while Boeing described that order as only an "initial tranche" of a potentially much larger transaction.

Beijing and Boeing have remained in prolonged negotiations over a deal that industry sources say could involve 500 737 MAX jets as well as dozens of wide-body aircraft.

The transaction has been stalled for years as Trump has threatened to restrict China's access to critical spare engine parts.

A major Boeing order would therefore offer Trump a high-profile example of US exports benefiting from his negotiations with Beijing, while giving China an opportunity to demonstrate progress on its economic priorities.

Technology and rare earths remain sticking points

The two sides are also expected to negotiate over technology restrictions and critical minerals.

Beijing has been pressing Washington to delay a rule that would prevent thousands of Chinese companies from accessing advanced US technology.

Washington, meanwhile, wants China to ease restrictions on shipments of rare earths and critical minerals that are essential to high-tech industries ranging from automobiles and aerospace to defence.

The issue highlights the increasingly interconnected nature of the US-China relationship.

While Washington wants to limit China's access to technologies considered strategically sensitive, US manufacturers remain dependent on supply chains involving Chinese minerals and processing capacity.

That creates incentives for both sides to negotiate, but also leaves significant room for disagreements over national security and industrial policy.

Taiwan poses a bigger geopolitical risk

Trade may produce the most visible announcements from the summit, but Taiwan could be the most sensitive issue.

US allies in Asia are increasingly concerned that Trump could soften Washington’s support for Taiwan in pursuit of economic agreements with Beijing.

Taiwan rejects China's sovereignty claims over the island.

The US, like most countries, does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, but remains its most important international backer and arms supplier.

Xi is expected to press Trump on Taiwan during the summit. Any change in Washington’s language could be closely scrutinised by governments across Asia.

"There's a great deal of trepidation, particularly from our allies, about where our China policy is going to land," said Emma Chanlett-Avery, political-security affairs director for US-based think tank Asia Society Policy Institute in an earlier Reuters report.

"Any indication of a softness on Taiwan would be quite alarming," she added.

Trump said Xi raised US arms sales to Taiwan during their May meeting.

Trump later described a pending weapons package worth as much as $14 billion as a "negotiating chip".

Beijing is also seeking a change in Washington's longstanding formulation on Taiwan.

People familiar with Chinese efforts told Reuters that Beijing hopes Trump will publicly state that the US opposes Taiwan's independence rather than simply saying Washington does not support independence.

The distinction could carry significant diplomatic weight, particularly for US allies that rely on Washington’s existing position as part of the regional security framework.

Iran adds another layer to the talks

The war in Iran creates another area of potential tension.

Trump is expected to ask Xi to use China's influence with Tehran to curb support for Iran.

China maintains close relations with Tehran and is by far the world's largest buyer of Iranian oil exports, giving Beijing an economic relationship with Iran that Washington believes could provide leverage.

China, however, has shown little inclination to use that influence in line with US demands.

Reuters reported last month that Beijing was selling billions of dollars' worth of goods to Iran through a sanctions-evasion scheme.

China's foreign ministry said it was not aware of such a scheme.

Washington has so far avoided directly targeting Chinese banks as part of its Iran pressure campaign.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stopped short of imposing penalties on Chinese banks when he unveiled an "economic onslaught" against Iran last month and warned countries to cut business ties with Tehran.

"To date, the American President seems content with China’s limited role, saying that the Chinese President had “behaved reasonably well.” This perceived restraint may not stem from Trump’s requests, but rather from Beijing’s calculus in maintaining ties with Gulf partners, including Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates," Toomas Hanso, junior research fellow at the International Centre for Defence and Security, said.

The Iran issue therefore gives Trump another reason to seek cooperation from Beijing, even as the two countries remain strategic competitors.

AI emerges as a new summit issue

Artificial intelligence is also expected to feature prominently when the leaders meet.

The highly anticipated Sept. 24 summit comes as some in the AI industry are calling for greater safeguards around the rapid development of advanced models.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week's state dinner with Trump and Xi, four people familiar with the event told POLITICO.

Their presence underscores the increasingly strategic role of AI in US-China relations.

Advanced AI models have implications not only for commercial competition but also for national security, military capabilities and control over critical technologies.

Analysts see AI as a potential area for cooperation because both countries face concerns over misuse and the broader risks created by rapidly advancing systems.

But the intense technological competition between Washington and Beijing is likely to limit the scope for substantive cooperation.

Any agreement on AI safeguards could therefore be largely symbolic, particularly as both countries continue to compete over chips, computing infrastructure, advanced models and access to the technologies needed to build them, Reuters said.

data.title: Invezz Explains: India wants UPI revenue but its payment data may be worth more
data.description:
India’s decision to introduce a merchant discount rate on selected UPI payments has reopened a debate over who should pay for the country’s digital payment infrastructure.

From October 15, person-to-merchant transactions above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300, while person-to-person transfers, smaller payments and small merchants remain protected.

The government says about 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected.

But the bigger question sits beyond the fee itself. UPI is not only a payments rail, but it is also creating digital transaction records that can help formalise businesses, improve credit assessment and give lenders a clearer view of cash flows.

That raises another question: as India starts monetising UPI directly, could the data generated by the network ultimately be worth more than the MDR revenue?

UPI’s value is no longer just in moving money

The scale is enormous. UPI processed 24.5 billion transactions worth about ₹29.82 lakh crore in August, according to NPCI data.

For banks and fintechs, a payment can have value beyond the few basis points earned for processing it.

Key takeaway

A reliable digital trail can show how frequently a merchant receives money, how stable those inflows are and whether sales are growing.

Indian policymakers have recognised this. Government material on digital public infrastructure says UPI has helped small businesses establish verifiable transaction histories, improving the ability of banks and fintechs to assess creditworthiness.

That does not mean UPI transaction data can simply be sold or repurposed. Lending and data-sharing remain subject to consent, privacy and regulatory safeguards.

But the financial footprint created by digital payments can become an underwriting input when accessed lawfully.

That matters in India, where many small businesses have historically lacked the financial records lenders prefer.

MDR solves one problem but could create another

The case for MDR is straightforward, as UPI costs money to operate.

Professor Ashish Das of IIT Bombay told Invezz that the network has a real operating cost.

“There is a cost for running the UPI system. The approximate cost can run into several thousand crores,” Das said.

He estimated annual costs could fall between ₹5,000 crore and ₹20,000 crore, while the new MDR system could generate roughly ₹15,000 crore. Those are estimates rather than audited figures, but they illustrate the funding problem.

Das said the economics depend on how closely MDR revenue matches the actual cost of running UPI. If revenue exceeds that cost, the system creates a profit pool; if it falls short, the funding gap remains.

ASSOCHAM President Nirmal K Minda told Invezz that MDR would make UPI more sustainable and support investment in infrastructure, fraud prevention and innovation.

Jyoti Prakash Gadia, managing director of Resurgent India, made a similar argument, saying the revenue could help banks and payment providers fund cybersecurity and expansion, although it may not fully recover investments already made in building UPI.

The hidden risk is losing valuable digital behaviour

The tension begins if merchants respond to MDR by changing behaviour.

Dr Manoranjan Sharma, chief economist at Infomerics Ratings, told Invezz that the legal incidence of the charge and its economic incidence need not be the same.

Merchants could absorb the cost, but they could also reduce discounts, raise prices or steer customers towards other payment methods. Sharma said consumers should watch for cash discounts, altered pricing and payment-specific incentives.

“If merchants raise broad prices rather than visibly charging UPI users, MDR becomes part of general operating costs and consumers may not identify its source,” he said.

Key takeaway

The bigger economic risk would emerge if some merchants shifted transaction volume back towards cash.

Previous government policy promoted low-value UPI partly because digital payments formalise transactions and create financial footprints that can improve access to credit.

A cash transaction produces far less usable information for a lender assessing business activity.

That makes the trade-off more complicated than MDR revenue versus merchant costs. India could gain a recurring source of funding for its payments network while weakening, at the margin, the data trail that makes the network useful for lending and formalisation.

The real prize may sit beyond payments

The new MDR framework does not necessarily undermine UPI’s data advantage. Most transactions remain outside the charge, and small merchants retain protections.

But policymakers now have two objectives to balance.

UPI needs sustainable economics for banks, apps and payment providers. It also needs merchants to keep choosing digital payments often enough for their transaction histories to remain useful.

Gadia told Invezz that the central challenge is ensuring higher ecosystem costs do not ultimately translate into higher consumer costs.

The same logic applies to data.

Key takeaway

The ₹15,000-crore revenue opportunity is visible and immediate. The value of millions of businesses building long-term digital financial histories is harder to put on a balance sheet.

For India, that less visible asset may ultimately prove more important.

The post Invezz Explains: India wants UPI revenue but its payment data may be worth more appeared first on Invezz

data.title: SpaceX stock forecast after hitting a $946 million NASA deal
data.description:
SpaceX stock has moved sideways at an important price, even after the company received a $964 million deal by NASA. SPCX also wavered as investors waited for the upcoming Starship Orbital test. It trades at $152, up by 47% from its lowest level this year. 

SpaceX stock wavers after reaching a NASA deal

SPCX stock wavered even after the company reached a big deal with NASA. In a statement, the agency awarded it three additional missions through a contract modification. 

The extension, worth about $946 million, will bring the number of missions to 17, and will help it maintain access to the space station. This amount includes ground, launch, in-orbit, and return and recovery operations. The total contract in this program is worth $5.92 billion.

SpaceX is seeing strong growth in its launch business. In its last earnings report, the company said that its space business brought in over $962 million in revenues, up from $746 million in the same period last year. 

The new contract comes as the company prepares to conduct its major Starship test on September 28. This test was initially scheduled for September 22nd, before it was moved to a later date. 

Elon Musk hopes that the new Starship will take the third version of its Starlink satellites in space. The new version will have 10x more capacity than the current one, allowing more speeds for end users. It will help it compete further with telecommunication companies like T-Mobile and AT&T. In a statement, Elon Musk said:

“Even if our monetization per bit dropped by a factor of 10, that would still mean a 10x increase in the revenue of Starlink. I think people are really underestimating Starlink here. This is a big deal.”

Starlink is the biggest cash earner for SpaceX. In its last earnings report, the company said that the connectivity business made over $4.29 billion, up sharply from the $3.2 billion it made last year. Its number of customers jumped to over 12 million, and the trajectory is accelerating. 

READ MORE: SpaceX stock outlook: where will SPCX be in the next five years?

SpaceX is becoming a big data center player

SPCX stock is also benefiting from the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. It runs Grok, a popular chatbot, and a large data center operation. It moved into the cloud services business, by providing access to its Colossus and Colossus II sites in the second quarter. This business contributed $1.6 billion in incremental revenue in the quarter. 

Most notably, the company continues to ramp up its data center operations and has already received some major orders. For example, the company recently inked a $1.1 billion-a-month deal with an unnamed client. It also received orders from companies like Anthropic, Google, and Reflection AI. 

This business explains why analysts believe that its revenue will continue growing in the near term. The average estimate is that its revenue will cross $150 billion next year, much higher than the $18 billion it made last year.

SpaceX stock price technical analysis

SPCX stock chart | Source: TradingView

The two-hour chart shows that the SPCX stock has soared in the past few weeks. It jumped from a low of $104.60 in August to the current $153. 

The stock formed an ascending triangle pattern, a common continuation sign in technical analysis. It has remained above the 50-period moving average. 

Therefore, the stock will have a bullish breakout, potentially to the next key level at $200.

data.title: Dow closes 110 pts lower as treasury yields rise and oil stays above $100
data.description:
US stocks ended mixed on Friday as investors wrapped up a volatile week marked by the Federal Reserve’s first interest-rate hike in three years, rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 114.74 points, or 0.22%, to 51,663.30, while the S&P 500 gained 11.53 points, or 0.12%, to 7,647.19.

The Nasdaq Composite advanced 92.72 points, or 0.35%, to 26,511.01.

The moves came as investors assessed the potential impact of a higher-for-longer interest-rate environment on equities and fixed-income markets. A semiconductor rally helped limit the pressure on broader US equities.

Treasury yields remain elevated

Treasury yields moved higher on Friday, adding to pressure on stocks.

The 10-year Treasury yield briefly climbed back above 5% after retreating on Thursday and was last up more than five basis points at 4.998%.

The benchmark yield had already risen above 5% earlier in the week, reaching its highest level since July 2007.

The move has kept inflation and interest-rate expectations in focus as investors assess the Federal Reserve’s next steps.

The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points this week, taking the target range to 3.75%-4%.

Markets are now pricing in more than a 50% probability of another rate increase at the central bank’s October meeting, up from 42.5% a week earlier and 7.2% a month ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

The prospect of additional rate increases could keep pressure on Treasury yields in the coming months.

Oil remains above $100 a barrel

Oil prices retreated on Friday but remained above $100 a barrel, keeping inflation concerns elevated.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 1.58% to settle at $100.30 a barrel, while Brent crude futures declined 0.91% to close at $103.87.

Crude prices eased from session highs after China, at Saudi Arabia’s request, asked Iran to limit attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi oil infrastructure.

However, oil remained at levels that could add to broader inflationary pressures.

Soaring oil prices have also pushed US diesel prices to record levels, potentially increasing costs across farming and shipping.

The combination of elevated oil prices and rising bond yields has added to concerns about the outlook for inflation and monetary policy.

Dow posts third weekly decline

Friday’s session ended the major indices on a mixed week. The Dow was down nearly 2% for the week, posting a third consecutive weekly decline and its worst weekly performance since March.

The S&P 500 was down 0.3% week to date, while the Nasdaq was up 0.3%, making it the only major index on track for a weekly gain.

Investors also monitored company-specific developments.

Berkshire Hathaway announced that Warren Buffett will step down as chairman and become chairman emeritus, nine months after handing the CEO role to Greg Abel.

Xenon Pharmaceuticals fell after temporarily pausing enrollment in clinical studies of an experimental drug following reports of side effects.

Cryptocurrency-linked stocks including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood surged as Bitcoin prices jumped.

The quarterly expiry of stock and index derivatives, known as triple witching, also contributed to late-session volatility.

data.title: Top crypto price predictions: Near Protocol, Venice Token, Hyperliquid
data.description:
The crypto market is doing well today, with most tokens being in the green, and the valuation hitting $2.76 trillion. This rally continued even after the Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan (BoJ) hiked interest rates, and as crude oil remained at an elevated level. This article provides a forecast for top tokens like Near Protocol (NEAR), Venice Token (VVV), and Hyperliquid (HYPE).

NEAR Protocol price forecast

NEAR Protocol is a top crypto project that runs a layer-1 network, a privacy-focused trading platform, and an AI agent marketplace. This positioning has helped it to perform well in the past few months, outperforming mainstream coins like Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP. 

The token continued rising this week, reaching a high of $3.7830, much higher than the year-to-date low of $0.8490. This surge makes it one of the top gainers in the crypto industry this year. 

The token has jumped above the key resistance level of $3.08, the upper side of the cup-and-handle pattern. This pattern normally leads to more gains since it is one of the most common continuation signs in technical analysis.

The token has jumped above all moving averages and the Supertrend indicator. At the same time, the Average Directional Index (ADX) has continued rising, a sign that the trend is gaining momentum. 

The risk, however, is that the token has become highly overbought, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) rising to 85. Therefore, there is a risk that the token will retreat and retest the support level of $3.08 and then resume the upward trend. This pattern is known as a break-and-retest pattern. 

NEAR price chart | Source: TradingView

Venice Token price forecast

Venice AI is a top project in the artificial intelligence industry, where it runs a platform that allows people to search different models, including from companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Grok. Users pay for the platform using fiat currency, with the company using part of the fees to buy and burn its tokens. It burned VVV tokens worth over $702k last month and has now burned $673k this month. 

Venice Token price has been in a strong rally this year and is hovering around its all-time high. It was trading at $27.25, a few points below the record high of $29.30. It remains slightly above the key resistance level of $21.48, the upper side of the cup-and-handle pattern. It has already formed a break-and-retest pattern.

The token has also remained above all moving averages. Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the token is upward, with the next key target to watch being at $35. 

VVV price chart | Source: TradingView

Hyperliquid price forecast

HYPE price has been in a strong upward trend after President Donald Trump signaled that he will support its entry into the United States. It also rose after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) supported tokenization of stocks in the United States. 

Hyperliquid is also seeing strong demand in its platform, with the volume in its perpetual DEX platform rising to over $240 billion in the last 30 days. This volume is much higher than its top peers like Aster and Lighter.

HYPE price chart | Source: TradingView

The token has also completed the formation of a break-and-retest pattern by falling back to $76, its highest level on June 16. It also moved above the key resistance level of $89.38, its previous all-time high. Therefore, the path of least resistance for the coin is upwards, with the next target being at $100.

data.title: Why is SanDisk stock gaining 8% today?
data.description:
SanDisk (SNDK) shares rose sharply on Friday as investors reacted to the company’s upcoming inclusion in the S&P 100 and continued strength in its financial performance.

The stock gained as much as 8.04% during Friday’s session.

The semiconductor company is set to join the S&P 100 before trading begins on Monday, September 21, replacing longtime index member Colgate-Palmolive.

SanDisk set to join S&P 100

The S&P 100 is a subset of the S&P 500 that includes some of the largest and most established companies in the broader index.

Companies seeking inclusion in the S&P 500 must meet requirements related to factors including market capitalisation, liquidity and profitability.

S&P Dow Jones Indices announced earlier this month that SanDisk would be added to the S&P 100, replacing Colgate-Palmolive.

The upcoming inclusion could increase demand for SanDisk shares in the short term as funds and exchange-traded products tracking the index adjust their holdings.

The buying related to the change may have contributed to Friday’s share-price move.

Over the longer term, however, the company's operating and financial performance is likely to remain a more significant factor for investors than its index membership.

The inclusion could also increase SanDisk’s visibility among institutional investors and add to the company’s profile as an established member of the broader US equity market.

Strong fiscal fourth-quarter results

SanDisk’s recent financial performance has provided another factor for investors to consider.

For its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, which ended July 3, the company reported revenue of $8.97 billion, representing a 372% increase from the same period a year earlier and a 51% sequential increase.

Diluted earnings per share came in at $43.97, compared with a loss in the prior-year period. EPS also increased 91% from the previous quarter.

The results come as demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications continues to support the semiconductor industry.

SanDisk has emerged as a beneficiary of the broader AI infrastructure buildout, with AI servers requiring significant amounts of high-speed NAND flash storage.

SanDisk shares are currently trading at about 24 times earnings and eight times forward earnings.

AI demand remains key focus

The outlook for AI-related semiconductor demand remains an important consideration for SanDisk investors.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly made bullish projections at an AI executive summit, saying chip sales in 2027 are expected to reach twice the level of 2026.

The projection reinforces expectations for continued demand for high-performance computing infrastructure, including memory and storage components.

SanDisk's exposure to NAND flash storage therefore places the company within the broader investment theme surrounding AI infrastructure spending.

Wall Street's stance also remains constructive.

Analysts have a consensus Buy rating on the stock, while the average 12-month price target is approximately $2,124.

With Sandisk preparing to enter the S&P 100 and reporting significant year-over-year and sequential revenue growth, investors will continue to focus on whether strong AI-related demand can support the company’s financial performance beyond the near-term boost associated with index inclusion.

The post Why is SanDisk stock gaining 8% today? appeared first on Invezz

data.title: BMO recommends betting on a recovery in this semiconductor stock
data.description:
MACOM Technology (MTSI) stock is inching higher on Friday after a senior BMO Capital analyst – Harsh Kumar – issued a bullish note in favour of the semiconductor firm.

In his research note, Kumar upgraded MTSI to Outperform and reiterated his $335 price objective, which signals potential upside of about 23% from current levels.

BMO’s bullish call brings much-needed reprieve to MACOM shares that are currently down some 30% versus their year-to-date high.

Why is BMO Capital bullish on MACOM stock

BMO highlights that the recent pullback presents an attractive entry point, as MTSI stock’s forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple compressed sharply from the high-50s in June down to about 29x.

More importantly, “fundamentals have remained rather solid throughout, driven by data center and industrial/defense," he added.

A major catalyst lies within the hyper-scaler buildout: massive capex from cloud service providers and artificial intelligence (AI) labs powering next-gen compute and networking infrastructure.

This is, in fact, expected to result in a 70% increase in MACOM’s data center vertical in 2026, an impressive acceleration from the 47% growth recorded in the prior fiscal year.

On Friday, the semiconductor stock broke above its 20-day moving average (MA), indicating the upward momentum could sustain in the near-term.

What else could drive MTSI shares higher?

Beyond cloud datacenters, MACOM shares are attractive because the firm’s broad-based portfolio is finding significant momentum in specialized industrial and defense applications.

According to the BMO analyst, defense demand “remains resilient and space becomes a material contributor to growth next year.”

With its advanced high-performance analog and RF products, MTSI is expanding its market share across satellite communication, radar, and next-gen telecom hardware.

Investors should also note that the semiconductor stock has a history of closing both October and November in “green” – a seasonal pattern that further improves its near-term appeal.

How Wall Street recommends playing MACOM

BMO’s constructive call mirrors broader sentiment across Wall Street, where institutional backing remains overwhelmingly positive.

LSEG data reveals that out of 19 analysts actively tracking MTSI shares, 15 maintain either a Buy or Strong Buy recommendation, with the remaining four assigning a Hold rating. None recommend selling.

With the mean Street price target currently hovering around $395, the broader consensus agrees that MACOM’s continued decline of about 30% from its late-May record high of $418.90 offers an attractive entry point if you’re interested in holding it for the longer term.

Supported by the strong fiscal fourth quarter (Q4) earnings outlook and robust institutional ownership above 76%, the stock appears strongly positioned to turn its recent operational momentum into an extended market recovery through the remainder of this year.

That said, MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings Inc does not currently pay a dividend, which makes it rather unattractive for income-focused investors in 2026.

data.title: Volkswagen stock plunges as €10B hit forces 2026 profit outlook cut
data.description:
Volkswagen shares fell 5% after slashing its 2026 profit outlook on Friday, citing a sharp contraction in China's car market, the rising cost of its job-cutting plan, and a major write-down on its stake in Porsche AG.

Europe's largest automaker now expects an operating return on sales of no more than 1% for the year, down from its previous guidance of 4% to 5.5%.

Shares fell as much as 7.5%, marking the stock's biggest intraday drop in a year, and the selloff spread to rivals BMW and Mercedes-Benz.

Where the €10 billion hit is coming from

Volkswagen said it expects negative effects totaling roughly €10 billion to weigh on this year's results.

A €6 billion write-down on the value of its Porsche AG stake accounts for a large share of that figure.

The rest reflects provisions tied to a hard-won agreement with workers reached this month, which will double Volkswagen's planned job cuts to 100,000 globally.

China remains the core problem

China, Volkswagen's largest market, continues to be the company's biggest drag.

China's overall car market has shrunk by more than a fifth through August this year, hit by an extended real estate crisis weighing on consumer spending.

The decline has hit Volkswagen even harder than the broader market, as the company struggles to offer electric vehicles competitive with local Chinese brands.

Volkswagen's own first-half results, reported earlier this year, showed the strain building well before Friday's announcement.

First-half revenue stood at €158.1 billion, while operating profit fell 11.6% to €5.9 billion, an operating margin of 3.8%, already below the low end of the company's prior full-year guidance range.

China sales fell 20% in the first half of 2026, the company said in July, even as electric vehicle orders in Europe rose more than 50% in the second quarter.

A guidance cut that keeps getting worse

Friday's announcement marks the second time this year Volkswagen has lowered its 2026 outlook.

In July, the company cut its expected sales revenue range to between a 3% decline and flat growth, while still maintaining its operating margin guidance of 4% to 5.5% at the time.

That guidance has now been abandoned entirely.

Volkswagen has also been grappling with underused plant capacity in Germany, adding to its cost pressures even as it pushes through a broader transformation program covering products, technology and its overall business structure.

Investors will now be watching whether Volkswagen can stabilize its China business and offset rising costs through its restructuring plan, or whether Friday's 1% target becomes the starting point for further cuts rather than a floor.

Operating return on sales has fallen every year since 2022, from around 8% that year to roughly 6% in 2023, near 5% in 2024, and just over 2% in 2025.

The originally guided 2026 range of 4% to 5.5% would have marked a rare improvement on that trend.

Instead, the updated 1% forecast makes 2026 set to be Volkswagen's weakest year for profitability across the entire period shown.

data.title: Strategy, Coinbase surge as Bitcoin hits $80k again, SEC eases tokenized trading
data.description:
Crypto-related stocks rose sharply on Friday as Bitcoin reclaimed the $80,000 level and investors responded to a new US regulatory framework for tokenized stocks.

Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) MSTR gained about 12%, while MARA Holdings rose 9%. Coinbase Global surged 10%, Galaxy Digital and Circle Internet Group each gained 7% and 6% respectively, while Robinhood Markets added 7.5%.

Bitcoin BTC climbed more than 5% to move above $80,000 for the first time in two weeks.

The cryptocurrency had spent recent weeks consolidating between roughly $75,000 and $78,000.

The gains came after the US Securities and Exchange Commission announced a five-year exemption that allows certain platforms to facilitate trading in blockchain-based or tokenized stocks and other securities.

SEC introduces five-year innovation exemption

The SEC's new "Innovation Exemption" provides tokenized securities venues with a five-year exemption from certain rules that apply to traditional stock exchanges, including the Nasdaq and New York Stock Exchange.

The exemption also covers certain liquidity providers, which will receive a five-year exemption from dealer registration requirements.

Tokenized stocks are digital representations of shares that can be traded on a blockchain.

The SEC said the framework is intended to address regulatory challenges that could otherwise make it difficult for platforms to comply with federal securities laws without potentially burdensome changes to their business models.

Platforms will have to notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their shares. They cannot offer the tokenized securities if the underlying issuer objects.

The SEC also said synthetic tokens that provide exposure to stocks through derivatives or other products will not be permitted under the exemption.

SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said the Innovation Exemption is intended to facilitate on-chain trading of certain tokenized stocks while maintaining investor protections and market integrity standards.

The exemption is set to expire five years after publication, while the SEC has invited public comments as it considers potential further changes.

Tokenized stocks could expand crypto platforms

The SEC said tokenized NMS stocks traded under the exemption must provide holders with the same rights and privileges as equivalent traditional shares, including dividend and voting rights.

Tokenized securities venues can trade eligible NMS stocks through permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools, although the SEC has imposed limits on the number of symbols and trading volume.

Venues must also stop trading a tokenized stock at the same time as trading in the underlying stock is halted on its primary exchange.

They must provide public information about their operations, trading activity, and the activities of their affiliates.

The crypto industry has argued that tokenization could change how financial markets operate by allowing shares to trade around the clock and settle transactions more quickly.

The SEC also highlighted potential benefits including greater liquidity, lower transaction costs, self-custody and fractional ownership.

Coinbase has previously signalled plans to offer tokenized stocks in the US when regulations permit.

Robinhood, Kraken and other crypto exchanges already offer tokenized stocks in overseas markets.

Coinbase gains from regulatory clarity

The SEC announcement came days after the US Senate failed to advance the broader CLARITY Act, leaving the cryptocurrency industry without the comprehensive market-structure legislation it had been seeking.

Against that backdrop, Baird reiterated a Neutral rating on Coinbase with a $130 price target, while describing the SEC's regulatory development as positive for the exchange.

Baird said the exemption could allow Coinbase to offer tokenized equities with full shareholder rights, bringing its asset offering more in line with Robinhood Markets.

The firm also cited a rebound in trading volumes and favourable regulatory activity, as well as Coinbase's continued development of its "Everything Exchange" strategy.

The SEC's decision could also create a path for crypto-native platforms to compete more directly with traditional brokerage businesses.

Analysts said tokenized equities could eventually bring platforms such as Coinbase and Robinhood into greater competition with established firms including Morgan Stanley's E*Trade and Charles Schwab.

For crypto-related stocks, Friday's gains therefore came alongside a regulatory development that could broaden the range of financial products offered through blockchain-based platforms.
